nom: The Ordinary Azelaic Acid Suspension 10% Cream for Redness and Blemish-Prone Skin

segments.dry: The one reviewer who names dry skin, alongside acne and rosacea, credits it with finally getting her skin glowing once added to her prescription routine; several other reviewers without dry skin themselves warn it can be too drying for dry skin, and at least one reviewer's skin dried out badly.
segments.oily: Reviewers with oily, acne-prone skin describe it as their go-to for minimizing oil and controlling shine, particularly under sunscreen and makeup, with one reviewer specifically advising it's best suited to oily rather than dry skin.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, including one whose oiliness shifts with the seasons, report it calms inflammation, prevents new breakouts, and helped her skin recover after her barrier was compromised by other treatments.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including some managing eczema, report no irritation and good results with fading spots and smoother texture, often using a moisturizer underneath as a buffer; no reviewer with sensitive skin reports a bad reaction.
segments.mature: The one reviewer who describes her skin as aging, in her mid-40s, says it saves her skin seasonally, especially in winter, though she finds it too much for her skin in the humid summer months.

concerns.dehydration: A number of reviewers say the formula can be drying, especially without a moisturizer layered on top or over dry skin specifically, with one describing her skin as badly dried out; most others report no dryness at all as long as they moisturize before or after application.
concerns.redness: This is the product's most consistently praised effect: reviewers with rosacea, perioral dermatitis, or general redness repeatedly report significant, sometimes dramatic fading of redness within weeks; no reviewer reports it worsening their redness under the current or original formula.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer used it specifically to help her compromised skin barrier recover after over-exfoliating, reporting calmer skin and fewer new breakouts within a week once she reintroduced it gently.
concerns.spots: Most reviewers report fading dark spots, sun spots, freckles, or acne scarring, typically over several weeks of consistent use; a few disagree, saying they couldn't use it enough to judge due to pilling issues, or that they saw no visible change to their pigmentation.
concerns.blemishes: The large majority of reviewers report fewer breakouts, calmer active acne, and smaller, less inflamed pimples within days to a couple of weeks; a notable minority disagree, describing new breakouts or increased blackheads, several tying this specifically to a formula change they say altered the product's smell and effectiveness.
concerns.oiliness: The two reviewers who mention oil control both report it helps minimize oiliness and shine, especially useful under sunscreen or makeup; neither reports it as insufficient for oil control.

aspects.libelle: Recent batches smell fishy or like onion

extraits.texte: I bought this to help with dark spots and dull skin but this dried out my skin so badly. Definitely only use if you have oily skin.

I cant speak to how well this product works for hyperpigmentation because it pills so horribly you literally cannot use any other products with it. And forget about wearing foundation over it! As someone who is 37 yo and struggling with hormonal acne, my other products are a non negotiable, so I rarely use this except occasionally on the weekends when I dont wear makeup. And when I do use it, it seems like I get an increase of blackheads a day later. Im glad this wasnt expensive because it mainly sits on my vanity taking up space lol. If you have a similar sitch as me, I highly recommend the acne kit from Tula; it also has azaleic acid in it, and has done wonders for my acne AND fading my acne scars.

I have dry skin, acne & rosacea. I've added this to my daily skin care to help with the redness. I use a prescription topical cream that wasn't cutting it alone for my rosacea, but with this added to everything - my skin finally is glowing!

I'm in my mid-40s w/ combo normal/oily skin in summertime, combo dry/normal skin in wintertime. This stuff saves my skin during the winter. During the summer I don't really use it, since our summers are super humid and HOT. That said, I can see how it could be too much for younger skin or oily skin, but for me, its really saves my skin seasonally!

As a black woman with oily, acne prone skin that has tried a ton of pricey products to fade my dark spots, I appreciate this product. I wouldn't say it's been the best in eliminating my post acne scarring, but it is my absolute go to for minimizing oily skin especially with sunscreen. Yes, it is sticky, but that really comes in handy for all night makeup. After cleansing, exfoliating, and using this? Omg even my drug store foundation applies like butter and wears like second skin. Yes yes yes.

extraits.titre: I wish I'd found this sooner
extraits.texte: I have combination hormonal acne-prone skin and I'm a licensed esthi. While I was in esthi school my barrier was suffering a bit, I was trying to re-introduce retinoids, and then unexpectedly in school we had to do 2 exfoliating treatments in a row including a chemical peel.... my skin reacted badly with a few cysts. I needed to give my barrier time to heal and then reintroduce a gentler active to help, and I chose to use azelaic acid. I started seeing results in as little as a week! It calmed my inflammation and prevented new breakouts. It's been a few months since that big breakout and now my skin has stayed calm thanks to regular use of azelaic, and I've been able to successfully reintroduce my retinoid too. And I've had no issues with the texture of this product. Love it!

Effective and gentle on my sensitive skin. My fair, freckled complexion is noticeably brighter, spots and freckles are significantly faded. I use daily in combination with the Ordinary Cold Pressed Rose Hip Oil, Moisturizer and Glycolic Acid toner.
